newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran starts electricity exports to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iran starts electricity exports to Turkey.

text.p: Iran started supplying electricity on Wednesday to Turkey under a deal which will deliver 150 million kilowatt hours a year of power to ease its western neighbour's serious electricity shortages.

State-run Tehran radio said the exports were being carried out under an accord signed during a visit to Iran this month by Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan. It did not say how much Turkey would pay for the exports.
Turkey and Iran signed several agreements during the visit, including a $23-billion landmark deal under which Ankara would buy Iranian gas for 22 years from 1999.
The gas deal came one week after a new United States sanctions law that penalises firms that invest $40 million or more a year in the oil and gas sectors of Iran or Libya.
A senior Turkish official has said Turkey would initially buy 25 megawatts of power from Iran, to be raised later in the year to 100 megawatts.
Turkey, in desperate need of power, is expected to face shortages later this year when demand peaks.

An Iranian Energy Ministry official has said that Iran sells 200 million kilowatt hours of power to Azerbaijan's enclave of Nakhichevan for $10 million a year and has signed a $50 million deal to provide one billion kilowatt hours annually to Armenia.
